overview.headline: How half life gives numeric ages to rocks and the geologic time scale

keyPoints.point: Minerals with natural radioactive elements let geologists calculate a rock numeric age in years
keyPoints.quote: Now we can use minerals that contain naturally occurring radioactive elements to calculate the numeric age of a rock in years.

keyPoints.point: Half life is the time needed for exactly half of parent atoms to decay into daughter atoms
keyPoints.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

keyPoints.point: Laboratory counts of remaining parent atoms and new daughter atoms are used to compute rock age
keyPoints.quote: Precise laboratory measurements of the number of remaining atoms of the parent and the number of atoms of the new daughter produced are used

keyPoints.point: Isotopically dated rock is paired with fossil bearing rock to assign relative and numeric ages
keyPoints.quote: a rock that can be dated isotopically is found together with rocks that can be assigned relative ages because of their fossils.
